page: Microsoft Azure F4-2amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine belonging to the Famdsv7 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The server features 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) with 1.0 thread per core, backed by 32.0 GB of system memory, which translates to a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance includes 472 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and is premium storage capable, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

Benchmark results indicate exceptional single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression all placing in the top tier (top 10%). However, multi-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores falling in the average (middle 50%) range. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compiling with clang are weaker, landing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth and database operations also perform at average levels.

The high memory-to-core ratio and dedicated CPU allocation provide strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The primary tradeoff is the low core count of 2 vCPUs, which limits multi-threaded scaling and makes it less suitable for heavy parallel compilation or ray tracing. This server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, single-threaded processing tasks, text processing, and moderate database operations.
